subject: Invite delivery heatmap + last-mile RSVP fallback plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.example.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invite delivery heatmap + last-mile RSVP fallback plan

Team —

Quick note after poking at the RSVP data from last week: we’re seeing a ~22% drop between email CTA click -> RSVP submit for a subset of recipients (mobile, a specific ESP). I attached a heatmap that highlights the problem windows. Before we start rewriting copy, I want a short triage + fallback plan so we can run a canary tomorrow.

Ask: please come back with the items below by EOD today so I can align legal/ops for the canary: 
- Root-cause hypothesis (one-liner) — Mateo
- UTM / redirect mapping sanity check + easy fix suggestions — Connor
- Proposed canary segmentation (audiences + percent) + staging for reminder sends — Marissa

Notes:
- Attachments: rsvp-heatmap.png (visual), utm-link-table.csv (current mapping)
- Proposed quick fix: avoid double-redirect on the registration CTA and append explicit utm_source=redwood-invite on the final landing URL. If that’s not trivial, we need a fallback that preserves the UTM query on the final redirect.

We’ll target a 5% canary to start (low-risk) and then 25% ramp if metrics look good. If possible include a short test that verifies the utm_source is present server-side after redirect.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Field Marketing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rsvp-heatmap.png (image, 384KB), utm-link-table.csv (CSV, 8KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.example.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.example.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invite delivery heatmap + last-mile RSVP fallback plan

On Wed, 4 Apr 2028 at 09:12 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example.com> wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Quick note after poking at the RSVP data from last week: we’re seeing a ~22% drop between email CTA click -> RSVP submit for a subset of recipients (mobile, a specific ESP). I attached a heatmap that highlights the problem windows. Before we start rewriting copy, I want a short triage + fallback plan so we can run a canary tomorrow.

Thanks Hannah — quick thoughts below, keeping this tight so we can ship the canary tomorrow: 

- Hypothesis: interstitial tracking/redirect chain is stripping utm_source for certain mobile browsers/ESP proxies. Also suspect a server-side redirect (3xx) without query preservation.
- Quick fixes (ranked):
  1) On the email CTA, append a final landing param: ?utm_source=redwood_invite. This guarantees the param on final URL even if redirects drop initial query.
  2) Update the redirect rule to preserve query strings (engineering config change, low-risk).
  3) If neither is feasible immediately, add a dedicated 1px tracking endpoint that sets a short-lived cookie and then issues a redirect with utm preserved (canary only).
- Canary segmentation:
  - Segment A (control): 5% - US engineers list - send via ESP-A (current path)
  - Segment B (canary): 5% - US engineers list - add explicit utm_source param on final link
  - Monitor: RSVP submit rate, registration page utm_source presence, and downstream GA events for 24h.
- Reminders: if canary holds, stagger reminders at +48h and +120h, with the second reminder only to those who opened but didn’t RSVP.

I’ll update the reminder-cadence-v2.docx and the spreadsheet in the link you shared. Will also add a quick QA checklist for the final redirect test.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Demand Manager
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: reminder-cadence-v2.docx (docx, 24KB)

From: Samir Patel <samir@cloudfoundry.example.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 08:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invite delivery heatmap + last-mile RSVP fallback plan

Hi Hannah / Marissa —

Thanks for the heads-up. We spotted the same behavior on our side this morning from recipients that arrived via the CloudFoundry digest. Two quick data points: 

1) Sample failing URL (click from mobile): https://rdrw.link/click?id=acme123 -> then redirects to https://events.cloudfoundry.com/reg?session=456 (no utm attached).
2) Server logs show the intermediate redirect (rdrw.link) issues a 302 without preserving the original query parameters in ~18% of mobile user agents.

I attached a screenshot from a user where the registration URL has no utm params. We can patch our side to preserve the query but sounds like adding the explicit utm_source at the final landing is the fastest mitigation.

We’re available for a quick sync at 10:30 PT if you want to triage live.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Events Ops Manager
CloudFoundry Events

---
Attachments: cf-registration-screenshot.png (image, 120KB)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.example.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@cloudfoundry.example.com>
Date: Sat, 6 Apr 2028 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Invite delivery heatmap + last-mile RSVP fallback plan

Team — thanks for the quick replies and Samir for the confirm. Final plan and owners below: 

1) Immediate mitigation (owner: Connor) — add explicit utm_source=redwood_invite to the final landing URL in the email CTA. Publish a short test page that echoes utm params so we can verify server-side. Target: deploy by 10:00 PT tomorrow (Apr 7).
2) Redirect fix (owner: Mateo) — update the redirect rule to preserve query strings on rdrw.link for known ESP user agents. Target: rolling deploy after small QA, ETA Apr 8.
3) Canary send (owner: Marissa) — 5% control vs 5% canary as outlined. Start canary after Connor confirms mitigation is live. Monitoring windows: 0-6h, 24h, 72h.
4) Reminders (owner: Marissa) — staggered: +48h (openers only), +5d (non-responders). Update reminder copy with clear CTA and include a second-line support link for registration issues.

Action items for today: 
- Connor: share a short verification test URL when the param is added (post the URL to the sheet link).
- Mateo: quick grep of redirect rules and one-line summary of fix (deadline EOD Apr 7).
- Marissa: prepare the canary list and schedule the send; include a HubSpot campaign id in the mapping doc.

If we can sign off on the canary metrics by Apr 9 we’ll do a 25% ramp the afternoon of Apr 10.

Please reply-all with confirmation once you have the owner tasks picked up.

Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Field Marketing
Redwood Inference
